PRJ-002.labour: Installation overtime ran 18% over — the same failure mode as the 2026 job.
PRJ-002.subcontractor: Rigging was committed on a rough estimate rather than a firm quote, and came back 19% higher.
PRJ-002.material: Broadly to plan; the small overrun is late-stage replacement stock.
PRJ-002.logistics: Held to budget under a single haulage contract.
PRJ-002.other: Permits and insurance came in under the allowance.

PRJ-003.labour: A compressed install window was absorbed entirely in overtime — 22% over budget.
PRJ-003.subcontractor: Quoted firm up front, so the overrun stayed in single digits.
PRJ-003.logistics: Slightly under; the site allowed direct delivery with no interim storage.

PRJ-004.material: Fabrication buys its materials up front, so this category leads the spend curve at 45% delivered.
PRJ-004.labour: Crew is on plan; installation hours have not started.
PRJ-004.logistics: Under budget — a single-site job with no haulage between venues.

PROJECT_LESSON.PRJ-002: Two of the three overruns here repeat on the 2026 job. Treat installation overtime and unquoted subcontract as a pattern for this project type, not bad luck.
PROJECT_LESSON.PRJ-003: Margin held five points better than Orchard Road because the subcontract was quoted firm. Labour was the entire gap.
PROJECT_LESSON.PRJ-004: Nothing is off plan. The spend curve is front-loaded by design — the test comes when installation labour lands.

INCIDENTS.title: LED module delivery received 8 days after order due date
INCIDENTS.detail: The installation window did not move, so the crew absorbed the delay. Replacement strip was expedited under AP-8834 to keep the arch lighting on programme.

INCIDENTS.title: Client added 3 arch spans after fabrication had started
INCIDENTS.detail: The amendment was accepted without a matching change to the contract value, so the added scope lands entirely on cost.

INCIDENTS.title: Backdrop fabric batch returned as faulty, panels re-made
INCIDENTS.detail: The material was credited in full, so the loss is not in material spend — it is in the 140 hours spent re-making and re-hanging the panels.

INCIDENTS.title: Orchard Road permit restricted works to 22:00–06:00
INCIDENTS.detail: Night-only access was a known condition of the road-closure permit. It was priced as normal hours in the budget, and worked as overtime.

INCIDENTS.title: Overtime with no supporting record in SAP B1
INCIDENTS.detail: 35 hours carry no incident, amendment or service call. This is stated rather than absorbed — an unexplained residual is a finding, not a rounding error.

INCIDENTS.title: LED module delivery received 11 days after order due date
INCIDENTS.detail: The identical failure recurred on the 2026 job with the same supplier. Replacement stock was expedited under PO-1975.

INCIDENTS.title: Canopy run extended after installation began
INCIDENTS.detail: Second consecutive festive job where scope moved after fabrication started.

INCIDENTS.title: Fixing batch returned — thread tolerance out of spec
INCIDENTS.detail: Credited in full; the cost is the re-drilling and re-fixing labour.

INCIDENTS.title: Two consecutive rain nights lost on the installation programme
INCIDENTS.detail: Recovered by working the following two nights at overtime rates.

INCIDENTS.title: Overtime with no supporting record in SAP B1
INCIDENTS.detail: 50 hours unexplained on a closed job — the record can no longer be reconstructed.

INCIDENTS.title: Venue brought the installation window forward by 6 days
INCIDENTS.detail: The whole programme compressed. This single amendment is the largest driver of the 22% labour overrun.

INCIDENTS.title: Fabric delivery received 7 days after order due date
INCIDENTS.detail: Landed into an already-compressed window, compounding INC-201.

INCIDENTS.title: Venue access restricted to 22:00–06:00 for public safety
